hotContext.criticalNews: Consumer HW4 FSD cycling through point releases: v14.3.6 introduced brake-stutter regression (July 28); v14.3.7 fix (2026.21.5) shipped August 1 and is in limited rollout (<1% fleet). Robotaxi fleet remains on early v15 builds (~40% of 7 planned improvement tracks). Consumer v15 OTA still end-2026/early-2027. Max-speed offset permanently removed.

recentKeyChanges.title: FSD v14.3.6 regressions reported widely; Tesla responds with v14.3.7 (2026.21.5) OTA fix
recentKeyChanges.description: Two distinct events bookend this research window. First, around July 28, Tesla Oracle and Teslarati documented owner reports of significant regressions in FSD v14.3.6 (2026.20.6.11): brake-stuttering / shadow-braking returned, with owners reporting unnecessary brake tapping, a blue tentacle constantly extending and retracting when confused by stationary pedestrians, left-lane camping, and highway-exit misses. The issues were notable enough to generate media coverage from multiple outlets even as Tesla continued widening the v14.3.6 rollout. Tesla responded by shipping FSD v14.3.7 in software package 2026.21.5, beginning rollout August 1. As of August 6, v14.3.7 was still in limited early-access distribution (less than 1% of HW4 fleet per TeslaFi). Release notes for v14.3.7 are nearly identical to v14.3.6 (same RL/MLIR/vision-encoder stack), but user reviews confirm the brake-stuttering regression is resolved; a highway-exit miss issue reportedly persists. Critical reality: Tesla shipping a regression-fix point-release within two weeks of a prior point-release is normal product cadence but signals ongoing instability in the v14.3.x branch at the very moment v15 robotaxi builds (still at ~40% completion) carry growing investor expectations. Consumer HW4 production software has now cycled v14.3.4 → v14.3.5 → v14.3.6 (regression) → v14.3.7 in roughly six weeks — incremental polish, not the architectural leap v15 represents.

positive_signals: Tesla responded quickly — v14.3.7 regression fix shipped approximately 10 days after v14.3.6 regressions were widely reported
v14.3.7 early-access users confirm brake-stuttering fixed; one reviewer noted zero instances of brake-stabbing, wheel-jerking, or unconfident movements
Rollout to early-access and influencer pool demonstrates active monitoring and fast iteration on v14.3.x branch
negative_signals: v14.3.6 introduced brake-stuttering / shadow-braking regression affecting multiple owners; Tesla Oracle and Teslarati documented complaints with video evidence
v14.3.7 release notes are nearly identical to v14.3.6 — no new capability, only regression patch; highway-exit miss reportedly still present
v14.3.7 still under 1% fleet rollout as of August 6 — most consumer HW4 owners remain on the regressed v14.3.6 build
Consumer production software remains on the v14.3.x branch — no v15 path visible in consumer OTA; v15 is fleet-only (robotaxi) at ~40% completion
Regression-then-patch cycle in v14.3.5 to v14.3.6 to v14.3.7 within six weeks signals instability as branch approaches its development ceiling

recentKeyChanges.title: Ashok: Tesla permanently removing FSD max-speed offset; will learn implied speed preferences instead
recentKeyChanges.description: During the research window, Tesla AI chief Ashok Elluswamy publicly confirmed that the manually configurable 'Max Speed' offset for FSD — which allowed drivers to set FSD to drive above posted speed limits — will not be reinstated. Ashok stated: 'Max speed control is an anti pattern' and confirmed Tesla is instead building systems that learn implied driver speed preferences from real behavior (e.g., when a driver taps the accelerator because FSD is too slow, the system logs and adapts). This was corroborated by Teslarati and NotATeslaApp. Context: Sweden and other EU regulators explicitly cited the manual speed offset toggle as a safety and compliance concern when urging rejection of FSD homologation. The permanent removal is simultaneously a regulatory concession and an architectural pivot toward behavior-inference. Critical framing: removing manual speed controls removes a disengagement trigger (owners frustrated by overly cautious speed) but also removes user agency over a core FSD behavior, generating community confusion. This is a software behavior decision — not a v15 milestone — but it affects how all current v14.x and future v15 builds interact with speed compliance.

positive_signals: Removing hard-coded speed offsets addresses a specific regulatory objection raised by Sweden and the EU — may unblock or accelerate EU homologation path
Behavior-inference approach (learning from accelerator taps) is architecturally more sophisticated than manual sliders and aligns with v15 AI-native design philosophy
NotATeslaApp and Teslarati both corroborate Ashok's statement
negative_signals: Decision removes driver control over speed — generates significant owner confusion and frustration per community feedback covered by Teslarati
Incorrect speed-zone data is a documented source of FSD disengagements in many regions; removing user override could increase disengagements until inference model matures
No timeline given for when implied-preference speed learning ships; current v14.3.7 still uses fixed speed behavior
